items.f: Sight glass not clearly visible / leaking and needs replacement.
items.r: Replace/repair sight glass. The gauge glass should be blown down once per shift to ensure it is working correctly and the standpipes do not become blocked with scale.

items.q: Gauge glass blown down each shift?
items.f: Gauge glasses are not blown down at the beginning of each shift.
items.r: The gauge glasses should be blown down once per shift to ensure that they are working correctly and that the standpipes do not become blocked with scale.

items.f: Water level Mobrey switches badly worn / water level control not ideal with slow response.
items.r: Upgrade the water level control system by installing a Spirax LP21 probe, controller and a VSD for the feedwater pump for modulating control of the water level.

items.q: Extra low water cut-out condition & test
items.f: Extra low water Mobrey worn / extra low water lock-out could not be verified.
items.r: Upgrade the extra low water protection by installing a Spirax LP40 probe and extra low water controller. Blow down every shift to check that the boiler trips and locks out at extra low water level.

items.f: Mobrey/level control blowdown pipework bent or damaged; blowdown not possible.
items.r: Replace/repair the sight glass and level control blowdown pipework as soon as possible.

items.q: Low / extra low / high water alarms (audible + visual)
items.f: Alarms for low and high water levels not correct: no audible low water alarm / no separate extra low alarm / no record kept of alarm tests.
items.r: All alarms, audible and visual, should be recorded. If the water level in the gauge glass is correct and a low water alarm persists, the level controls should be checked; if the level remains low, check the feedwater pumps.

items.f: Records of alarm tests could not be provided for review.
items.r: Record all alarm tests in the daily logbook and retain records for review.

items.f: Feedwater pump faulty / cannot keep up with steam demand / no automation of feedwater pumps.
items.r: Urgent attention should be paid to malfunctioning boiler feedwater pumps and to the automation controls of the feedwater pumps.

items.f: No feedwater pump protection is installed on the pumps.
items.r: Install feedwater pump protection to prevent pump damage.

items.f: No feedwater flow meter installed / feedwater meter not working.
items.r: Install a feedwater flow meter (magnetic type recommended) for each boiler to monitor the amount of water used per boiler.

items.q: Cabling to level switches / transmitters secure
items.f: Cabling to feedwater pumps, level switches and/or transmitters is not secure and safe.
items.r: Cabling to feedwater pumps, level switches and/or transmitters should be secured and made safe.

items.f: Boiler does not have automatic TDS control / TDS system not working due to seized valves or faulty controller.
items.r: Automatic TDS controls and water sample coolers need to be installed/upgraded on the boiler. TDS levels must be maintained between 2500-3000 to prevent water carry-over to the process.

items.f: TDS measurement was extremely high, measured above specification with handheld tester.
items.r: Maintain TDS between 2500-3000 by correct blowdown and dosing. Record TDS and pH for each shift in the daily logbook.

items.f: No water sample cooler installed on the boiler.
items.r: Install a water sample cooler for safe and accurate boiler water sampling.

items.f: Boiler blowdown valve leaking / stiff / blowdown pipe blocked.
items.r: Repair/replace the blowdown valve. Blowdown valve flanges must be tight with effortless action.

items.f: Steam leak on safety valves / safety valve test records not available.
items.r: Replace or overhaul safety valves with steam leaks. Safety valves to be tested with the AIA inspector and documented.

items.f: Steam leak on the crown valve.
items.r: Replace/repair the leaking crown valve as soon as possible.

items.f: Feedwater valve / check (one-way) valve passing or seized.
items.r: Replace the feedwater isolating and check valves.

items.f: Boiler pressure gauge faulty / not calibrated.
items.r: Replace the boiler pressure gauge with a newly calibrated pressure gauge.

items.f: Copper pipes used for boiler safety instruments; does not comply with BS EN 12953. High pressure lock-out drifting from set calibration.
items.r: Replace copper instrument pipework to comply with BS EN 12953. Replace/recalibrate the high pressure safety lock-out and incorporate the pressure transducer onto the new pipework.

items.f: Air release valve leaking / seized.
items.r: Repair/replace the air release valve.

items.f: Fire tubes blocked / not cleaned regularly, reducing heat transfer.
items.r: Fire tubes should be cleaned regularly, ideally every three to four months, to maintain optimum heat transfer and boiler efficiency.

items.f: Refractory is cracked/damaged which leads to loss of heat and efficiency.
items.r: Repair/recast the damaged refractory.

items.f: Smokebox door clamps/bolts missing; smokebox seals leaking.
items.r: Replace all missing smokebox door clamps/bolts and repair smokebox seals. Smokebox doors must be tight.

items.f: Exit flue gas temperature gauge not working; monitoring of blocked tubes and combustion efficiency not possible.
items.r: Replace the exit flue gas temperature gauge to monitor fire tube blockage and combustion efficiency.

items.f: Boiler instrumentation not calibrated.
items.r: Calibrate or replace boiler instrumentation.

items.f: Control panel switches, buttons and pilot lights damaged or not working; wiring loose with risk of electrocution.
items.r: Upgrade the panel with a new OEM automated control panel with HMI screen (and fan VSDs where applicable) compliant with pressure equipment regulations and EN boiler safety standards.

items.f: Safety interlocks could not be verified / not tested.
items.r: Yearly AIA safety inspections to be done: safety chain lockouts, low water alarm and lock-out, safety valves and E-stop to be tested and documented.

items.f: The AIA hot commissioning report for the setting of safety limiters was not provided for review.
items.r: Provide AIA inspection and hot commissioning records. The boiler must be subjected to internal and external inspection annually as required by law.

items.f: Weekly or monthly maintenance schedules could not be provided for review.
items.r: Implement daily, weekly and monthly maintenance schedules for the boiler plant, steam distribution and condensate recovery equipment, and record all maintenance.

items.f: Fuel analysis records were not provided for review.
items.r: Perform a proximate analysis, a mineral ash analysis and ash fusion temperatures at least once per coal delivery. Ensure the volatile content of fuel is within specification.

items.q: Combustion quality (red coals off stoker end?)
items.f: Incomplete combustion of fuel was occurring with red coals being discharged off the end of the stoker.
items.r: Set up combustion controls, check undergrate air distribution and grate speed to ensure complete burnout before the end of the grate.

items.f: The boiler could not maintain the operating pressure setpoint.
items.r: Investigate combustion controls, fuel quality and heating surface fouling; restore automatic control of ID and FD fans.

items.f: The stoker mat shows signs of overheating with damaged links and bent link rods; ends of link rods damaged with drifting rods and missing split pins.
items.r: Replace damaged links and link rods and fit split pins. Use OEM parts only.

items.f: The stoker mat could not be tensioned due to excessive wear on drive links.
items.r: Replace worn drive links; remove a link from the stoker chain and jack the motor to correct tension.

items.f: The stoker needs to be levelled in the boiler; the stoker frame shows signs of distortion.
items.r: Level the stoker in the boiler and repair/replace the distorted frame sections.

items.f: Guillotine doors not level; guillotine castings/refractory damaged; door height not displayed / encoder faulty.
items.r: Repair guillotine doors and castings; replace the guillotine door level indicator/encoder.

items.f: Air leaks found on the ignition arch; ignition arch seal rope damaged.
items.r: Replace ignition arch seal rope and close air leaks to prevent cold air cooling the ignition arch.

items.f: Draught pipework to the ignition arch missing/damaged with no feedback to the Photohelic; no automatic control of ID and FD fans.
items.r: Repair draught pipework; replace the Photohelic with a Yokogawa pressure controller for automatic furnace pressure control.

items.f: No swinging chute installed; air leaks from the coal hopper.
items.r: Install a swinging chute between the overhead fuel hopper and the stoker hopper. This also prevents air leaks at the coal hopper.

items.f: The stoker hoppers and shut-off doors need replacement; air leaks found on the coal hopper.
items.r: Replace stoker hoppers and shut-off doors; seal air leaks.

items.f: Undergrate damper actuators not installed / not working.
items.r: Install/repair undergrate damper actuators for correct air distribution along the grate.

items.f: Stoker motor misaligned, chain loose and slipping, V-belts loose with slippage, no V-belt cover.
items.r: Align the stoker motor, tension the chain, replace and tension V-belts and install a V-belt cover.

items.f: FD fan actuator missing / damper control poor.
items.r: Install a VSD to control the FD fan speed instead of damper and actuator for better control of air flow.

items.f: ID damper actuator not working.
items.r: Install a VSD for ID fan speed control. VSDs give finer, more accurate control than actuator-driven dampers.

items.f: No O2 probe/analyser installed; monitoring of efficient combustion is not possible.
items.r: Install a Lamtec LT2 O2 analyser per furnace and reduce flue gas oxygen content by adjusting the fuel trim and automating combustion control.

items.q: Temperature probes (ignition arch, rear roller, coal hopper)
items.f: Ignition arch / rear roller / coal hopper temperature probes not installed or broken.
items.r: Install/replace the ignition arch, rear roller and coal hopper temperature probes.

items.f: Spy holes and air leaks around the stoker allow cold air in, cooling the ignition arch.
items.r: Close spy holes and air leaks around the stoker to prevent cold air cooling the ignition arch.

items.f: No moisturising steam introduced into the coal in the stoker hopper.
items.r: Introduce moisturising steam into the coal in the stoker hopper; this assists the fine fuel fraction to adhere and burn properly.

items.f: Grit collector blocked/dirty; internals worn; wedge plates not sealing on the grit trolley causing air ingress.
items.r: Clean out the grit collector, replace the internals and re-align the wedge plates so they seal tightly onto the grit trolley.

items.f: The grit arrestor pressure drop cannot be monitored as differential pressure gauges are not installed.
items.r: Install differential pressure gauges on the grit collectors and boilers to indicate the level of blockage.

items.f: Grit trolleys, ash chute trolleys and ash chute doors damaged/leaking.
items.r: Repair and replace leaking/damaged ash chute doors, grit collector double flaps and trolleys.

items.f: Sootblowers not working.
items.r: Repair sootblowers and operate per the maintenance schedule.

items.f: Emission test records not available.
items.r: Emission tests to be completed.

burner.section: Fuel / HFO Handling — Burner (data entry + condition)

items.q: DATA: Required fuel temperature at burner (spec)
items.f: (entry field, deg C)
items.r: (no recommendation - data only)

items.q: DATA: Required fuel pressure at burner (spec)
items.f: (entry field, bar)
items.r: (no recommendation - data only)

items.q: DATA: Fuel pump control type (dropdown: VSD / DOL / Ring main / Pressure regulator / Other)
items.f: (entry field)
items.r: (no recommendation - data only)

items.q: MEASURED: Actual fuel temperature at burner
items.f: Actual fuel temperature measured at ___ deg C, outside the required specification, negatively affecting atomisation and combustion.
items.r: Repair/replace fuel heaters and heat tracing and restore the fuel temperature to specification for proper atomisation.

items.q: MEASURED: Actual fuel pressure at burner
items.f: Actual fuel pressure measured at ___ bar, outside the required specification, negatively affecting combustion stability.
items.r: Restore the fuel supply pressure to specification. Install/set a separate pressure regulator for the burner and keep the ring main at constant pressure.

items.f: Fuel pump worn/leaking and requires attention.
items.r: Service or replace the fuel pump.

items.q: Fuel pump VSD / motor control condition
items.f: Fuel pump VSD/motor control faulty or not in use; pump running uncontrolled.
items.r: Repair or replace the VSD/motor control for stable fuel supply pressure and efficient pump operation.

items.f: Records of the last burner service were not provided.
items.r: Maintain records of burner services and work done. A bi-annual burner service is recommended to run burners at optimal efficiency.

items.f: Leaking of HFO was observed at the burner / oil leaking into the cup on standby due to worn internal seals of the fuel block.
items.r: Overhaul the burner fuel block with a full service kit and seal all oil leaks on burners and oil lines to prevent energy loss, safety hazards and contamination.

items.f: Burner cup not properly cleaned as needed (every start of shift).
items.r: Clean the atomiser cup at the start of every shift and include it in the operator duties.

items.f: Atomiser belt comes off at start-up: belt tension too high and motor/atomiser pulleys misaligned.
items.r: Align motor and atomiser pulleys, set correct belt tension and keep a spare belt on site. Replace the belt if worn.

items.f: Burner quarl/refractory cracked or worn.
items.r: Replace burner quarl/refractory at the next service (refractory bricks and cement available from John Thompson).

items.f: Burner head air cone worn / vanes and ducting fouled.
items.r: Clean and inspect burner vanes, swirler cup and ducting; replace worn components.

items.f: Primary air ducting leaking (temporarily sealed with tape); air leaks on ducting and smoke doors.
items.r: Repair all air leaks on ducting and smokebox doors to maintain proper combustion air control; replace ducting where required.

items.f: Primary/secondary air damper linkages loose or movement restricted.
items.r: Tighten and free up damper linkages so movement is clear and unrestricted; check actuator calibration.

items.f: Ignition assembly damaged; gas pipe nozzle broken and temporarily repaired.
items.r: Replace the damaged ignition components; reroute cabling to minimise damage and wear.

items.f: Flame scanner failing / not detecting flame at low fire due to fuel quality, causing lockouts.
items.r: Clean/replace the flame scanner, tidy and reroute cabling, and address fuel quality to ensure reliable flame detection at low fire.

items.f: Heat tracing on burner oil lines damaged and not working.
items.r: Replace the heat tracing on the burner and ring main oil lines and insulate the oil lines properly.

items.f: Minimum air pressure switch faulty / airline blocked.
items.r: Replace the minimum air pressure switch and clean/reroute the airline. Burner ignition must be prevented when air pressure is not present.

items.f: Primary air differential switch faulty / airlines blocked or damaged.
items.r: Replace the differential air pressure switch; the burner must lock out if the primary air chamber differential is not balanced at ignition.

items.f: Door hinge limit switch damaged; burner does not lock out when the door is opened.
items.r: Replace the door open limit switch so the burner locks out when the door is opened.

items.f: The ring main does not maintain constant pressure, negatively impacting combustion stability and burner efficiency.
items.r: Resolve oil pressure fluctuations in the ring main. Install a separate pressure regulator for the burner and keep the ring main at a constant pressure so operators need not adjust supply pressure when switching between boilers.

items.f: No O2 analyser installed / reference air pump and filter defective, affecting accuracy of oxygen readings.
items.r: Install/replace the O2 analyser with a Lamtec LT2 KS1D-HT probe and control panel for improved combustion monitoring and control.

items.f: Flue gas oxygen content outside the optimal range.
items.r: Reduce the flue gas oxygen content to between 3% and 6% by adjusting the fuel/air ratio. Yearly combustion set-ups should be done for optimal combustion efficiency.

items.f: No fuel flow meter installed / HFO flow meter not working; fuel consumption not recorded.
items.r: Install/replace the fuel flow meter to monitor and record fuel consumption.

items.f: Fuel storage area untidy and fuel exposed to rain, increasing the moisture content of the fuel.
items.r: Store biomass fuel under cover and keep the storage area clean to control moisture content and fire risk.

items.f: Fuel moisture content is high and the fuel contains contaminants (sand, stones, metal), reducing combustion efficiency and damaging the grate.
items.r: Control fuel moisture (typically below 30-35% for grate firing) and screen out contaminants. Record fuel moisture daily.

items.f: Fuel feeding system worn, blocking or feeding irregularly.
items.r: Repair the fuel feeding system and set up feed-rate control linked to steam demand.

items.f: Fuel level control in the metering bin is not working; fuel supply to the furnace is irregular.
items.r: Repair the metering bin level sensors and feed control.

items.q: Burn-back / fire protection on fuel feed
items.f: Burn-back protection not working or not installed, posing a fire risk in the fuel feed system.
items.r: Install or repair burn-back protection (rotary valve or double flap, feed chute temperature sensor and water quench) and test it regularly.

items.f: Grate bars worn, warped or missing, causing an uneven fuel bed and poor air distribution.
items.r: Replace worn or damaged grate bars and restore correct grate movement and speed settings.

items.f: Clinker formation on the grate is restricting combustion air.
items.r: Remove clinker; check the fuel ash content and furnace temperatures and adjust primary air and grate speed to prevent clinker forming.

items.f: Primary and secondary air dampers are not working or not controlled, resulting in incomplete combustion.
items.r: Repair the dampers and actuators and set up primary/secondary air distribution for complete combustion.

items.f: Furnace refractory is cracked or damaged.
items.r: Repair the damaged refractory.

items.f: Furnace pressure is not controlled, with a risk of smoke and flame blow-back.
items.r: Repair the furnace pressure transmitter and ID fan control to maintain a slight negative furnace pressure.

items.f: FD/ID fans are controlled by dampers only or the VSDs are faulty.
items.r: Install or repair VSDs on the FD and ID fans for accurate combustion air control.

items.f: No O2 analyser installed; combustion efficiency cannot be monitored.
items.r: Install an O2 analyser and set combustion for the fuel fired (typically 6-8% O2 for biomass).

items.f: High unburnt fuel in the ash, indicating incomplete combustion.
items.r: Adjust grate speed, fuel bed depth and air distribution to reduce unburnt fuel in the ash.

items.f: Furnace temperature probes not installed or faulty.
items.r: Install or replace the furnace temperature probes.

items.q: Ash removal system (screw / conveyor / wet ash)
items.f: Ash removal system blocked, worn or leaking.
items.r: Repair the ash removal system and schedule regular cleaning.

items.f: Grit arrestor / multi-cyclone blocked or worn and the differential pressure is not monitored.
items.r: Clean the grit arrestor / multi-cyclone, replace worn internals and install differential pressure gauges.

items.q: Spark arrestor / fire risk in flue path
items.f: No spark arrestor; sparks are carried over into the flue path.
items.r: Install a spark arrestor upstream of any filter equipment to prevent fires.

items.f: Visible smoke at the stack, indicating incomplete combustion.
items.r: Adjust combustion settings and complete emission testing.

items.f: Heating surfaces fouled and sootblowers not working.
items.r: Repair the sootblowers and clean the heating surfaces regularly.

items.f: Operating pressure and distribution issues noted (describe).
items.r: Review steam system operating pressures and distribution; install shut-off valves on the main steam manifold where missing.

items.q: Steam traps installed & trap set composition
items.f: The steam trap sets consist of only an isolation valve before the steam trap.
items.r: Each trap set should consist of: two isolation valves (one on either side), strainer before the trap, steam trap, sight glass and check valve.

items.f: Most steam traps are functional but some are passing steam, seen from the feedwater storage tank overfilling and steam flow from the tank vent.
items.r: Carry out an in-house audit to determine whether the correct traps are selected and sized; replace damaged traps; set up and maintain a steam trap database; test traps at least once a year and record all maintenance.

items.f: Condensate return pipework unlagged on some return lines.
items.r: All condensate return pipework should be lagged and clad and returned to the feedwater storage tank. Install bypass valves to allow contaminated condensate to be dumped.

items.f: Make-up water is not being softened as the unit is not working.
items.r: Repair, replace or have your local supplier investigate the water softener units and chemical dosing. Customer to supply service report.

items.f: Chemical dosing pumps installed but chemicals are not being introduced into the feedwater storage tank.
items.r: Restore chemical dosing. Regular inspection of the chemical drums is required and must be noted in the operator's logbook to prevent the boiler being operated without the required chemicals.

items.f: Water treatment service reports need to be supplied for review.
items.r: A local water treatment specialist must make regular visits to ensure operators and laboratory technicians maintain correct chemical dosing and boiler blowdown.

items.f: TDS and pH are not measured and recorded daily.
items.r: TDS and pH levels must be recorded for each shift in the daily logbook.

items.f: Chemical spillage present on feedwater storage tank and pipework.
items.r: Clean chemical spillage and repair the source; protect the tank and pipework from corrosion.

items.f: Hotwell tank and pipework leaking and heavily rusted / feedwater temperature too high due to condensate return.
items.r: Repair/replace the hotwell tank and pipework; manage feedwater temperature to protect the feedwater pumps.

items.f: Steam pipework inside the boiler house is damaged or missing lagging.
items.r: Repair all damaged lagging and cladding; lag all unlagged pipework inside the boiler house and the steam pipework to each process.

items.f: Valves and flanges inside the boiler house are unlagged.
items.r: Lag all valves and flanges inside the boiler house and between the boiler house and process plants.

items.f: Feedwater storage tank lagging shows spillage and wear; no cladding on feedwater lines.
items.r: Lag the feedwater tank and feedwater lines to the boiler.

items.f: Condensate return pipework is unlagged on some return lines.
items.r: Lag the condensate return pipework.

items.q: Steam/water leaks in boiler house & distribution
items.f: The following steam leaks were noted: (list locations).
items.r: Replace and repair leaking valves and components as soon as steam and water leaks occur; repair pipework with steam leaks.

items.f: There is 0% condensate return - a significant loss due to wasted water and heat not returned to the feedwater storage tank.
items.r: Automate and repair the condensate return system; check all steam traps to ensure they are not passing steam; install a meter for monitoring condensate return/loss to calculate the cost of steam production.

items.f: Operators do not record the required 4-hourly readings.
items.r: Record every 4 hours: boiler water TDS and pH; blowdown; feedwater TDS, pH, hardness, pressure and tank level; softener online; bags of salt added; brine tank level; stack smoke appearance; flue gas exit temperature.

items.f: Shift blowdown checks of gauge glass and level controls not performed.
items.r: Blow down every shift to check the boiler trips and locks out at extra low water level; ensure operators measure and record all required readings.

items.f: Operators not adequately trained on the equipment.
items.r: Operators must be trained to safely operate the equipment.
